newsitem.title: UK: T&N says U.S. court rejects Georgine appeal.
newsitem.headline: T&N says U.S. court rejects Georgine appeal.

text.p: British engineering group T&N Plc said on Wednesday that the U.S. Supreme Court had rejected its appeal to allow future asbestos claims to be settled under the terms of the so-called Georgine class action.
After months of deliberation the U.S. courts decided against T&N's case which could have potentially brought down the cost of its exposure to liabilities from such claims.

But T&N said in a statement released in London late on Wednesday that its existing provisions and insurance meant the company was already fully covered and that the failure of its Georgine appeal would have "no financial consequences which are not already allowed for".
The news helped send T&N's shares spinning lower, despite the company stating that it was fully covered for claims, regardless of whether there was a positive outcome for the appeal
But the share price fall -- down nearly 10 percent to 144 pence -- reflected market disappointment that potential savings would not be realised.

In March chairman Colin Hope had told Reuters: "The way we have done the provisioning at the moment, we have assumed the Georgine appeal fails....If it doesn't there is about 100 million stg less possibly needed than we previously thought."
The group has sought to clear the decks on claims by putting into place 441 million pounds of provisions and a further 500 million of insurance cover against any future asbestos claims.
The ruling ends months of legal wrangling in the U.S. But the judgement which came this afternoon is not the only factor weighing on shares, say analysts.
Danny Bevan, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, told Reuters the court case "just adds to disappointment that a takeover bid has not materialised".
T&N had been rumoured to be a takeover target earlier this month with Dana Corp and Federal Mogul Corp both cited as possible suitors.
The relentless advance of sterling against the mark has also continued to act as a depressant on many export-led engineering stocks.
But on the court judgement, Bevan concluded that the concerns may be overblown because "all known liabilities are provided for".
